Alex — thanks for the clear ask. I put together a concise MAP draft and a companion smoke-test spreadsheet for your team to sanity-check. High level below; full MAP attached.

Summary (top-line):
- Business success anchors:
  1) 95% intent-recognition accuracy on the 3 pilot flows (billing, referral, triage) measured over 10k sample queries.
  2) 20–25% reduction in average handling time for Triage flows vs baseline within 4 weeks of pilot start.
  3) Demonstrable ROI signal: pilot must show cost per resolved conversation <= $1.00 at production QPS projections.

- Technical exit gates:
  - P95 generation latency <= 450ms on dedicated instance profile (seq length 512) under target concurrency.
  - KV/prefix caching validated: cold-start token penalty <= 15% vs warm baseline across representative session traces.

- Sandbox smoke tests (minimum):
  1) 50 scripted prompts per flow, golden-label pass rate >= 90% for top-1 intent.
  2) End-to-end latency harness (10 concurrent sessions) — must meet P95 SLA above.
  3) Data flow verification: no PHI persisted to logs, KMS-wrapped keys used in ingestion pipeline.

Timeline (proposed):
- Week 0: MAP sign-off + initial data handoff
- Week 1–2: Sandbox provisioning + smoke-test run 1
- Week 3–5: Iteration on prompts & model config + smoke-test run 2
- Week 6–8: Canary routing with limited traffic + operational runbook handoff
- Week 9–12: Production roll (if pass), post-roll metrics review

I've attached: MAP-draft-starlite_v1.pdf and starlite-smoke-tests-v1.xlsx.

Next steps I propose: 30-minute sync Monday to walk through acceptance thresholds and who signs off on each gate (technical, product, procurement). Does 10am PT work?

Thanks — IRENE
Irene Choi

Looping in a couple of operational notes from infra and product engineering:

- Fallback plan suggestion: configure smart-routing policy with a cost-tier fallback (primary: high-accuracy q4 quant model on dedicated pool; fallback: lower-cost quantized model on burst pool) + throttling rules at the ingress to prevent NVMe swap. Expected behavior documented in the MAP addendum.
- Concurrency spike behavior: we'll run a stress profile (1x, 2x, 4x target QPS) and capture P95/P99 curves. If P95 breaches the 450ms threshold at 2x, the gate will be "degraded-mode acceptable" only if business metric (handled conversations per hour) remains within 85% of baseline.
- Labels: recommend a 3-layer labeling approach — (1) golden labels by SME for 2k seed set, (2) automated weak labels over historical logs, (3) calibration set for final acceptance.

Ben
